newsitem.title: MACAU: Macau gears up to celebrate Hong Kong's handover.
newsitem.headline: Macau gears up to celebrate Hong Kong's handover.

text.p: Chinese community leaders in Macau have set up a committee to celebrate the return of the nearby British colony of Hong Kong to China on July 1, a committee spokesman said on Wednesday.

The presidium of the Macau Compatriots Organising Committee for the Celebration of Hong Kong's Return to the Motherland includes casino mogul Stanley Ho, prominent businessman Man Man Kei and Catholic Bishop Dom Domingos Lam.
The committee also has representatives of major business, labour and community organisations.

The Macau Daily News, Beijing's semi-official mouthpiece in the territory, said in an editorial that the committee would "serve as a basis for preparing the festive activities of Macau's return (to China in 1999)".
The Portuguese-run territory, which Lisbon has ruled since 1557, will revert to Chinese administration in December 1999, two-and-a-half years after Hong Kong's handover.
The lead up to Macau's handover has been much smoother than that for the the British colony.

Lisbon long ago renounced sovereignty over the tiny enclave, making Macau a Chinese territory under Portuguese administration, and Beijing's views are already sought on all major decisions regarding it.
